messages.subject: two-group “added growth” LGM?
parts: I would like to look at the difference in a latent slope between two groups using the “added growth” technique, which involves (1) adding an additional latent slope variable identical in form to the LV of interest, but to only one of the two groups, and (2) constraining all parameters in common between the two groups to be equal. I can't figure out how to do either of these things in lavaan. Is it possible?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: two-group “added growth” LGM?
parts:
Greg,

I haven't run a model like this before, but it should be easy enough.  If a parameter is constrained to equality across groups, you only need to label that parameter once (see "intercept" and "slope" below), but for different parameters for each group, you can use the c() function to constrain (or NA/label, if free) the parameter for each group.  Here, I am forcing the loadings onto the "added" growth slope to be zero for the first group, but 0-1-2-3 for the second group (or use whatever values you would use for the "slope" loadings).  I imagine you would also fix the (co)variance to zero in the first group, since they are in effect "missing" that construct altogether.

addGrowth <- "
         intercept =~ 1*t1 + 1*t2 + 1*t3 + 1*t4
         slope =~ 0*t1 + 1*t2 + 2*t3 + 3*t4
         added =~ c(0, 0)*t1 + c(0, 1)*t2 + c(0, 2)*t3 + c(0, 3)*t4

         ## change NA to 0 if you do not want the "added" growth slope to be correlated with the common intercept/slope
         added ~~ c(0, NA)*added + c(0, NA)*intercept + c(0, NA)*slope

         ## use a single label for a free parameter to constrain across groups.  It works the same as: intercept ~~ c(psi11, psi11)*intercept
         intercept ~~ psi11*intercept + psi21*slope
         slope ~~ psi22*slope
"

The documentation available on the lavaan site has a PDF and a link to Yves' article in the Journal of Statistical Software, both of which demonstrate model syntax for multiple groups.

http://lavaan.ugent.be/?q=node/14

Terry

messages.subject: Re: two-group “added growth” LGM?
parts:
My problem is that what I have generally typed in as the “model” is incomplete, relying on lavaan to fill in the missing (co)variances and intercepts. Yet, if I understand the requirements of this methodology, those all have to be equalized between groups as well. After playing with lavaanify() a bit, here's what I've come up with for a semi-complicated example:
lavaanify(
"i.VABIL ~ ed + amnart s.VABIL ~ ed + amnart VABIL.1 =~ flu_let.1 + flu_cat.1 VABIL.2 =~ flu_let.2 + flu_cat.2 VABIL.3 =~ flu_let.3 + flu_cat.3 i.VABIL =~ 1*VABIL.1 + 1*VABIL.2 + 1*VABIL.3 s.VABIL =~ 0*VABIL.1 + 1*VABIL.2 + 2*VABIL.3;x.VABIL =~ c(0,0)*VABIL.1 + c(0,1)*VABIL.2 + c(0,2)*VABIL.3;x.VABIL ~ c(0,NA)*ed + c(0,NA)*amnart",ngroup=2,meanstructure = TRUE, int.ov.free = FALSE, int.lv.free = TRUE, auto.fix.first = TRUE, auto.fix.single = TRUE, auto.var = TRUE, auto.cov.lv.x = TRUE, auto.cov.y = TRUE,group.equal=c("loadings", "intercepts", "means","thresholds", "regressions", "residuals", "residual.covariances", "lv.variances", "lv.covariances"),group.partial=c("x.VABIL~1","x.VABIL~~x.VABIL","x.VABIL~ed","x.VABIL~amnart"))

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: two-group “added growth” LGM?
parts: On 12/01/2012 01:37 AM, Greg Shenaut wrote:

> The procedure is also described in Chapter 5 of Duncan, Duncan, &
> Strycker, An Introduction to Latent Variable Growth Curve Modeling:
> Concepts, Issues, and Applications 2nd Ed. (2006). They use EQS.

Ok, I had a look at this. Below is the syntax (Example 5.2). This is
just one of many possibilities. Using the 'lavaan' function (instead of
growth) is probably more elegant. But the chi-square test statistic
seems to match the value reported in the book. The 'trick' is to include
the 'add' factor in both groups, and constrain the factor loadings to
zero in the first group.

Yves.


# Example 5.1: Multiple-Sample Analysis of Change
MEAN.G1 <- c(1.4435, 1.7231, 1.8312)
lower1 <- ' 1.764
0.933 2.291
0.856 1.645 2.355 '
COV.G1 <- getCov(lower1, names=c("v1","v2","v3"))

MEAN.G2 <- c(1.5545, 1.8648, 2.2804)
lower2 <- ' 1.941
0.978 2.223
0.901 1.645 2.729 '
COV.G2 <- getCov(lower2, names=c("v1","v2","v3"))

model5.1 <- ' constant =~ 1*v1 + 1*v2 + 1*v3
linear =~ 0*v1 + 1*v2 + 2*v3
'
fit5.1 <- growth(model5.1, sample.cov=list(COV.G1, COV.G2), mimic="EQS",
sample.mean=list(MEAN.G1, MEAN.G2), sample.nobs=c(196,95),
group.equal=c("means","residuals",
"lv.variances","lv.covariances"))
summary(fit5.1, standardized=TRUE)


# Example 5.2: Alternative Multiple-Sample Analysis of 'Added Growth' LGM

model5.2 <- ' constant =~ 1*v1 + 1*v2 + 1*v3
linear =~ 0*v1 + 1*v2 + 2*v3
add =~ c(0,0)*v1 + c(0,1)*v2 + c(0,2)*v3

# manual syntax for latent means
constant ~ c(a1,a1)*1
linear ~ c(b1,b1)*1
add ~ c(0,NA)*1

# zero covariance with constant/linear
add ~~ 0*constant
add ~~ 0*linear

'
fit5.2 <- growth(model5.2, sample.cov=list(COV.G1, COV.G2), mimic="EQS",
sample.mean=list(MEAN.G1, MEAN.G2), sample.nobs=c(196,95),
group.equal=c("residuals",
"lv.variances","lv.covariances"))
summary(fit5.2, standardized=TRUE)
